1	# Generative AI's Act Two: From Technology Hammer to Real Value
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://www.sequoiacap.com/article/generative-ai-act-two/
     5	
     6	Published September 20, 2023 by Sonya Huang, Pat Grady and GPT-4 (Sequoia Capital)
     7	
     8	## The Foundation: Decades of Convergence
     9	
    10	Generative AI's emergence is not a sudden event but the culmination of decades of technological progress:
    11	
    12	- **Six decades of Moore's Law** delivered the compute horsepower to process exaflops of data.
    13	- **Four decades of the internet** (accelerated by COVID) produced trillions of tokens of training data.
    14	- **Two decades of mobile and cloud computing** put a supercomputer in every human's palm.
    15	
    16	ChatGPT's launch was the spark that ignited a Cambrian explosion of innovation not seen since the early internet. AI researchers became rockstars, hacker houses overflowed with autonomous agents and companionship chatbots, and the arXiv printing press became so prolific that researchers jokingly called for a pause on publications.
    17	
    18	But excitement quickly turned to hysteria. Every company became an "AI copilot." Inboxes filled with undifferentiated pitches for "AI Salesforce" and "AI Adobe." The $100M pre-product seed round returned. Cracks appeared: artists challenged machine-generated IP, Washington debated regulation, and a whisper spread that generative AI was not actually useful — products fell short of expectations with terrible user retention.
    19	
    20	## Early Commercial Traction Despite Skepticism
    21	
    22	Despite the discontent, generative AI has had a more successful commercial start than SaaS, with **>$1 billion in revenue from startups alone** — a milestone that took SaaS years, not months, to reach. Standout successes include:
    23	
    24	- **ChatGPT**: Fastest-growing application in history, with strong product-market fit among students and developers.
    25	- **Midjourney**: Reported hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue with a team of just 11 people.
    26	- **Character.ai**: Popularized AI entertainment and companionship; users spend an average of **2 hours per session** in-app.
    27	
    28	However, these successes don't change the reality that many AI companies lack product-market fit or sustainable competitive advantage.
    29	
    30	## The Retention Problem: AI-First Apps vs. Incumbents
    31	
    32	Mobile app retention data reveals a stark gap between established consumer apps and AI-first companies:
    33	
    34	### User Retention Comparison (Mobile Apps)
    35	
    36	| App | Category | Retention Rate |
    37	|---|---|---|
    38	| WhatsApp | Incumbent | 85% |
    39	| Instagram | Incumbent | 64% |
    40	| YouTube | Incumbent | 64% |
    41	| TikTok | Incumbent | 60% |
    42	| Snapchat | Incumbent | 51% |
    43	| Roblox | Incumbent | 41% |
    44	| Tinder | Incumbent | 34% |
    45	| Candy Crush | Incumbent | 32% |
    46	| Duolingo | Incumbent | 30% |
    47	| **Incumbent Median** | — | **51%** |
    48	| Character.ai | AI-First | 41% |
    49	| Runway | AI-First | 27% |
    50	| Remini | AI-First | 14% |
    51	| ChatGPT | AI-First | 14% |
    52	| Lensa | AI-First | 12% |
    53	| **AI-First Median** | — | **14%** |
    54	
    55	![Retention comparison: Incumbents vs AI-First Companies](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    56	
    57	A separate monthly active usage benchmark for incumbents shows even higher engagement bars:
    58	
    59	| App | Monthly Active Usage |
    60	|---|---|
    61	| YouTube | 85% |
    62	| Instagram | 73% |
    63	| TikTok | 69% |
    64	| Snapchat | 67% |
    65	| WhatsApp | 63% |
    66	| Roblox | 61% |
    67	| Tinder | 54% |
    68	| Duolingo | 50% |
    69	| Candy Crush | 48% |
    70	| **Median** | **63%** |
    71	
    72	![Monthly active usage benchmarks for incumbents](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    73	
    74	## From Act 1 to Act 2
    75	
    76	Sequoia frames the generative AI market as transitioning between two phases:
    77	
    78	**Act 1 (Technology-Out):** The discovery of foundation models as a new "hammer" led to a wave of novelty apps — lightweight demonstrations of cool technology. These apps used foundation models as the entire solution and often lacked stickiness.
    79	
    80	**Act 2 (Customer-Back):** The emerging phase focuses on solving human problems end-to-end. Key characteristics of Act 2 companies:
    81	
    82	- Use foundation models as **a piece** of a more comprehensive solution, not the entire product
    83	- Introduce **new editing interfaces** that make workflows stickier and outputs better
    84	- Are often **multi-modal** in nature
    85	- Solve problems **end-to-end** rather than offering thin wrappers
    86	
    87	Examples of Act 2 companies: **Harvey** (custom LLMs for elite law firms), **Glean** (crawling and indexing workspaces for relevant enterprise AI), **Character** and **Ava** (digital companions).
    88	
    89	The updated Sequoia generative AI market map is now organized **by use case rather than model modality**, reflecting the evolution from technology hammer to actual value delivery and the increasingly multi-modal nature of applications.
    90	
    91	## Key Findings
    92	
    93	- **Generative AI startups exceeded $1B in revenue faster than SaaS**, proving real commercial demand despite hype-cycle skepticism.
    94	- **AI-first apps face a severe retention gap**: 14% median retention vs. 51% for incumbent consumer apps — a 3.6x disadvantage.
    95	- **The market is shifting from Act 1 (technology-out) to Act 2 (customer-back)**, where foundation models become components of comprehensive, workflow-integrated solutions rather than standalone products.
    96	- **Multi-modal, end-to-end problem solving** and new editing interfaces are the hallmarks of companies likely to win in Act 2.
    97	- **Character.ai is the retention outlier** among AI-first apps at 41%, approaching incumbent levels, suggesting that companionship/entertainment may be generative AI's strongest consumer use case.

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RgbColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
from lxml import etree
import os

# Create presentation 16:9
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# Color palette - Sequoia-inspired professional
DARK_BG = RgbColor(0x1A, 0x1A, 0x1A)
WHITE = RgbColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHT_GRAY = RgbColor(0xF5, 0xF5, 0xF5)
MEDIUM_GRAY = RgbColor(0x88, 0x88, 0x88)
DARK_GRAY = RgbColor(0x44, 0x44, 0x44)
ACCENT_RED = RgbColor(0xA5, 0x2A, 0x2A)  # Sequoia-ish deep red
ACCENT_GREEN = RgbColor(0x2E, 0x7D, 0x32)
INCUMBENT_BAR = RgbColor(0x4A, 0x90, 0xA4)  # muted teal
AI_BAR = RgbColor(0xA5, 0x2A, 0x2A)  # deep red
MEDIAN_BAR = RgbColor(0x66, 0x66, 0x66)

def add_background(slide, color=DARK_BG):
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18, bold=False, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return txBox

def add_multiline_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, lines, font_size=16, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, line_spacing=1.2, font_name="Calibri"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = line
        p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.alignment = align
        p.space_after = Pt(font_size * (line_spacing - 1))
    return txBox

def add_shape_text(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=14, bold=False, color=WHITE, fill_color=None, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    if fill_color:
        shape.fill.solid()
        shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    else:
        shape.fill.background()
    shape.line.fill.background()
    tf = shape.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.alignment = align
    tf.paragraphs[0].space_before = Pt(0)
    return shape

# ============================================
# SLIDE 1: Title Slide
# ============================================
slide1 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])  # blank
add_background(slide1, DARK_BG)

# Top accent bar
accent = slide1.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.15))
accent.fill.solid()
accent.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT_RED
accent.line.fill.background()

# Title
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(2.2), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.5),
            "Generative AI's Act Two", font_size=54, bold=True, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri Light")

# Subtitle
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(3.4), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.8),
            "From Technology Hammer to Real Value", font_size=32, bold=False, color=LIGHT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri Light")

# Attribution
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(5.0), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.6),
            "Sequoia Capital  |  September 2023", font_size=18, bold=False, color=MEDIUM_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri")

add_textbox(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(5.5), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.6),
            "By Sonya Huang, Pat Grady and GPT-4", font_size=14, bold=False, color=MEDIUM_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri")

# ============================================
# SLIDE 2: Decades of Convergence
# ============================================
slide2 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_background(slide2, WHITE)

add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
            "Six Decades of Technological Progress Converged to Enable Generative AI",
            font_size=28, bold=True, color=DARK_BG, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri Light")

# Timeline bars
bar_y = Inches(2.0)
bar_height = Inches(0.6)
bar_widths = [Inches(10.5), Inches(7.0), Inches(3.5)]
bar_colors = [RgbColor(0x5E, 0x35, 0x35), RgbColor(0x8D, 0x6E, 0x63), RgbColor(0xBC, 0xAA, 0xA4)]
labels = ["6 decades of Moore's Law", "4 decades of the Internet", "2 decades of Mobile & Cloud"]
sublabels = [
    "Compute horsepower to process exaflops of data",
    "Trillions of tokens of training data (accelerated by COVID)",
    "A supercomputer in every human's palm"
]
durations = ["60 years", "40 years", "20 years"]

for i, (bw, bc, lbl, sub, dur) in enumerate(zip(bar_widths, bar_colors, labels, sublabels, durations)):
    y = bar_y + i * Inches(1.4)
    shape = slide2.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.8), y, bw, bar_height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = bc
    shape.line.fill.background()
    # label inside bar
    add_textbox(slide2, Inches(1.0), y + Inches(0.08), bw - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.5),
                f"{lbl}  —  {dur}", font_size=18, bold=True, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    add_textbox(slide2, Inches(1.0), y + Inches(0.7), bw, Inches(0.5),
                sub, font_size=14, bold=False, color=DARK_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Bottom context
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.5), Inches(12), Inches(0.6),
            "ChatGPT's launch ignited a Cambrian explosion of innovation not seen since the early internet.",
            font_size=16, bold=False, color=DARK_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri")

# ============================================
# SLIDE 3: GenAI Outpaces SaaS
# ============================================
slide3 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_background(slide3, WHITE)

add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
            "GenAI Startups Surpassed $1B Revenue Faster Than SaaS Ever Did",
            font_size=28, bold=True, color=DARK_BG, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri Light")

# Big stat
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.4), Inches(5), Inches(1.0),
            ">$1B", font_size=72, bold=True, color=ACCENT_RED, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri Light")
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.6), Inches(2.3), Inches(5), Inches(0.5),
            "in startup revenue alone", font_size=18, bold=False, color=DARK_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.6), Inches(2.8), Inches(5), Inches(0.5),
            "A milestone that took SaaS years, not months, to reach.", font_size=14, bold=False, color=MEDIUM_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Standout examples boxes
examples = [
    ("ChatGPT", "Fastest-growing application in history. Strong product-market fit among students and developers."),
    ("Midjourney", "Hundreds of millions in revenue with a team of just 11 people."),
    ("Character.ai", "Users spend an average of 2 hours per session in-app.")
]
box_y = Inches(1.5)
box_w = Inches(3.6)
box_h = Inches(2.2)
box_x_start = Inches(6.0)
for idx, (title, desc) in enumerate(examples):
    x = box_x_start + idx * Inches(3.9)
    shape = slide3.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, x, box_y, box_w, box_h)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = LIGHT_GRAY
    shape.line.color.rgb = RgbColor(0xDD, 0xDD, 0xDD)
    add_textbox(slide3, x + Inches(0.2), box_y + Inches(0.2), box_w - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.5),
                title, font_size=20, bold=True, color=DARK_BG, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    add_textbox(slide3, x + Inches(0.2), box_y + Inches(0.8), box_w - Inches(0.4), Inches(1.2),
                desc, font_size=14, bold=False, color=DARK_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Bottom caution
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.5),
            "However, these successes don't change the reality that many AI companies lack product-market fit or sustainable competitive advantage.",
            font_size=14, bold=False, color=MEDIUM_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri")

# ============================================
# SLIDE 4: Retention Gap (Side-by-Side Bar Chart)
# ============================================
slide4 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_background(slide4, WHITE)

add_textbox(slide4, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.3), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
            "AI-First Apps Show 14% Median Retention vs. 51% for Incumbents",
            font_size=26, bold=True, color=DARK_BG, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri Light")

# Data
incumbents = [
    ("WhatsApp", 85), ("Instagram", 64), ("YouTube", 64), ("TikTok", 60),
    ("Snapchat", 51), ("Roblox", 41), ("Tinder", 34), ("Candy Crush", 32), ("Duolingo", 30)
]
ai_first = [
    ("Character.ai", 41), ("Runway", 27), ("Remini", 14), ("ChatGPT", 14), ("Lensa", 12)
]

chart_left = Inches(0.6)
chart_top = Inches(1.2)
chart_width = Inches(12.0)
chart_height = Inches(5.2)

bar_max_w = Inches(4.5)
bar_h = Inches(0.42)
row_gap = Inches(0.52)
left_col_x = Inches(1.0)
right_col_x = Inches(7.3)
col_label_y = Inches(1.15)

# Column headers
add_textbox(slide4, left_col_x, col_label_y, Inches(4.5), Inches(0.4),
            "Incumbents", font_size=18, bold=True, color=INCUMBENT_BAR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide4, right_col_x, col_label_y, Inches(4.5), Inches(0.4),
            "AI-First Companies", font_size=18, bold=True, color=AI_BAR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Median labels
add_textbox(slide4, left_col_x, col_label_y + Inches(0.35), Inches(4.5), Inches(0.3),
            "Median: 51%", font_size=12, bold=True, color=MEDIUM_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide4, right_col_x, col_label_y + Inches(0.35), Inches(4.5), Inches(0.3),
            "Median: 14%", font_size=12, bold=True, color=MEDIUM_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Draw incumbent bars
for i, (name, val) in enumerate(incumbents):
    y = chart_top + Inches(0.5) + i * row_gap
    bw = bar_max_w * (val / 100.0)
    shape = slide4.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left_col_x, y, bw, bar_h)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = INCUMBENT_BAR
    shape.line.fill.background()
    add_textbox(slide4, left_col_x + bw + Inches(0.1), y, Inches(1.5), bar_h,
                f"{val}%", font_size=13, bold=False, color=DARK_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    add_textbox(slide4, left_col_x, y + Inches(0.02), Inches(2.5), bar_h,
                name, font_size=12, bold=False, color=DARK_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Draw AI-first bars
for i, (name, val) in enumerate(ai_first):
    y = chart_top + Inches(0.5) + i * row_gap
    bw = bar_max_w * (val / 100.0)
    shape = slide4.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, right_col_x, y, bw, bar_h)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = AI_BAR
    shape.line.fill.background()
    add_textbox(slide4, right_col_x + bw + Inches(0.1), y, Inches(1.5), bar_h,
                f"{val}%", font_size=13, bold=False, color=DARK_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    add_textbox(slide4, right_col_x, y + Inches(0.02), Inches(2.5), bar_h,
                name, font_size=12, bold=False, color=DARK_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Bottom insight
add_textbox(slide4, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.6), Inches(12), Inches(0.5),
            "A 3.6× retention disadvantage for AI-first apps — the critical gap Act 2 must close.",
            font_size=15, bold=True, color=DARK_BG, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri")

# ============================================
# SLIDE 5: Incumbent Monthly Usage
# ============================================
slide5 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_background(slide5, WHITE)
